slides.0.subtitle: Pisco, South Africa, California and Armenia
slides.1.title: Pisco: Peru and Chile
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Peruvian pisco
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Eight authorised varieties (Quebranta, Mollar, Uvina, Negra Criolla; Italia, Moscatel, Torontel, Albilla); single distillation, no water or additives afterwards, no oak ageing, resting at least three months in inert vessels; 38–48% (Difford's Guide, GuildSomm)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Three types
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Puro from a single variety; Acholado from blended musts; Mosto Verde distilled from partly fermented must that retains natural sugar, at lower yield
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Chilean pisco
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Coquimbo and Atacama were delimited in 1931; oak ageing and dilution with water are allowed, with pot and column stills; grades run Tradicional, Especial, Reservado and Gran Pisco (GuildSomm)
slides.1.content: Peru and Chile still dispute the Pisco name, so the lesson compares rules only.
slides.2.title: South Africa and California
slides.2.highlights.0.title: South African brandy
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Pot-still brandy must be 100% pot-still (since 2014), aged at least three years in oak of 340 L or less, at least 38%; Vintage blends 30–80% pot-still with matured wine spirit, all at least eight years; Blended needs at least 30% pot-still (Wine With Seth, SA Brandy)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Grapes and areas
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Chiefly Chenin Blanc and Colombar; Paarl, Stellenbosch, Robertson, Worcester and the Klein Karoo; KWV was formed in 1918
slides.2.highlights.2.title: California
slides.2.highlights.2.content: US brandy may use any grape and any equipment; Germain-Robin was created in 1982 by Cognac native Hubert Germain-Robin with Ansley Coale (Cigar Aficionado)
slides.2.content: The New World trait is looser rules and a wider range of styles.
slides.3.title: Armenia and the Caucasus
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Yerevan origins
slides.3.highlights.0.content: In 1887 the merchant Nerses Tairyan (Tairov) founded a distillery in Yerevan; master blender Mkrtich Musinyants joined in 1900 and his Fine-Champagne Otborny was recognised at the 1902 Bordeaux exhibition (Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Modern rules
slides.3.highlights.1.content: A 1999 national standard requires Armenian brandy to be made in Armenia from local grapes; Ararat's age range includes Ani (7 years), Akhtamar (10) and Vaspurakan (15)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Scope note
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Detailed rules for Georgia and other Caucasus areas were not verified in our sources; they are only a pointer to an existing tradition and are not tested
slides.3.content: The Churchill and Ararat story is a legend and is left out.
May Peruvian pisco be diluted with water after distillation?
A. Distilled from partly fermented must
One difference between Chilean and Peruvian pisco?
A. Chile allows oak ageing and dilution
C. Chile uses only red grapes
What is the cask size cap for South African pot-still brandy?
340 L or less, for at least 3 years.
How long must all components of South African Vintage brandy age?
A. Hubert Germain-Robin and Ansley Coale, 1982
